<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Complete Algorithm and Additional Implementation Details</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S3" title="3 ZoomGain Data Construction Pipeline ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> describes the core pipeline.
Here we add two implementation details, incorporated into Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ Joint crop/full-image audit and rewriting. ‣ Appendix A Complete Algorithm and Additional Implementation Details ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.
Model assignments and thresholds are given in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Construction Settings ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>;
the prompts are collected in Appendix <a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Prompts Used in Data Construction ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Anchor markers in the zoomed view.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The expanded crop <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{z}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{z}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> may contain several objects of the anchor’s category.
A VLM enumerates these instances, including partially visible ones, and matches the selected anchor to its grounded box.
If multiple instances are present, we draw a red rectangle around the anchor itself;
if only one is present, the crop remains unmarked.
This rectangle is distinct from <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, which marks the entire crop region in the global view.
The marked-view caption prompt uses it only to identify the anchor and otherwise follows the unmarked-view instructions.
It must not be described as photographed content or used as an answer.
Local questions may refer to the marker; global questions use natural referring expressions.
Figure <a href="#A1.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Joint crop/full-image audit and rewriting. ‣ Appendix A Complete Algorithm and Additional Implementation Details ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows both cases.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Joint crop/full-image audit and rewriting.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After QA generation, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">EDGE_REWRITER</span> inspects the crop and the full photograph with <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> marked,
together with both question forms and the reference answer.
It checks whether answer-bearing text or objects continue beyond the crop,
whether the global referent is unique, and whether both questions admit the same answer.
It returns <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">keep</em>, <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">rewrite</em>, or <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">drop</em>.
A bounded rewrite can add answer-free qualifiers valid in both views while preserving the non-OCR answer.
For OCR, it may narrow the question and answer to a complete text block or specified prefix/suffix
contained in the original answer, but cannot add text read from the full image.
Counting questions whose requested set extends outside the crop are discarded.
Revisions are synchronized across the local/global and English/Chinese questions,
and target and answer constraints are checked again before crop-based verification
(Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Quality Verification and Multi-Source Distractors ‣ 3 ZoomGain Data Construction Pipeline ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).
Both anchor enumeration and this audit use Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A1.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/anchor_marker_examples.png" id="A1.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:343/257;" width="343" height="257" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span><span id="A1.F4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Conditional anchor markers in the zoomed view.</span>
(a) Two people are present, including the partially visible person on the left;
the red rectangle selects the person wearing a red-and-black plaid shawl.
(b) Only one person is present, so no marker is added.
Both views are rendered from the original images and recorded crop/anchor coordinates
using the pipeline’s marker and resizing functions.
The rectangle identifies the anchor rather than the answer-bearing detail;
it is used only in the zoomed view and is not part of the photographed scene.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> <span id="alg1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ZoomGain Data Construction</span></figcaption>
<div id="alg1.6" class="ltx_listing ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom ltx_listing">
<div id="alg1.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">1:</span>
              
              
            Image pool <math id="alg1.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{I}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℐ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{I}</annotation></semantics></math>; configured models; <math id="alg1.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=10</annotation></semantics></math> samples per model; <math id="alg1.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R=3</annotation></semantics></math> MCQ verification rounds

</div>
<div id="alg1.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">2:</span>
              
              
            Verified QA dataset <math id="alg1.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> with evidence regions and distractor provenance

</div>
<div id="alg1.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">3:</span>
              
              
            <math id="alg1.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}\leftarrow\emptyset" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}\leftarrow\emptyset</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">4:</span>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Notation and operations.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> records the anchor instances; <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{V}_{z}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>V</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{V}_{z}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the optionally marked zoomed view.
<span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">EdgeAuditAndRewrite</span> returns a verdict <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> and the retained or revised QA under the constraints above.
Both question forms have English and Chinese versions.
The remaining operations follow Section <a href="#S3" title="3 ZoomGain Data Construction Pipeline ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, with verification settings in
Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Construction Settings ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>; <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> preserves distractor provenance during repairs.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>

</span></td>

<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Verification Thresholds.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All verification stages sample 10 answers per model.
Crop-based verification requires at least 6 correct answers from each of its two models,
Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct and Kimi-K2.6.
Blind verification rejects a question only when all three models each answer correctly at least 3 times.
Final MCQ verification requires at least 6 correct selections from each of its three models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Verification Rounds and Distractor Repair.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Final MCQ verification uses at most three rounds:
an initial check followed by up to two further checks after distractor repairs.
Each round applies the per-model threshold described above.
Candidates that still fail after the final round are discarded.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Benchmark Question Categories</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The three question categories in ZoomGainBench cover the following fine-grained details.
Figures <a href="#A3.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ Attribute Recognition. ‣ Appendix C Benchmark Question Categories ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>–<a href="#A3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Text Recognition (OCR). ‣ Appendix C Benchmark Question Categories ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> show three examples per category,
with paired English and Chinese questions.
The orange boxes mark the specific details needed to answer each question,
with dashed lines connecting them to enlarged views.
These boxes are selected for illustration and are distinct from the pipeline’s anchor boxes.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Attribute Recognition.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Questions concern a target’s color, material, shape, object identity,
actions, or relations.
The examples below ask about a truck’s mirror housing, a glass tabletop,
and a small logo on a golfer’s visor.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F5" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/benchmark_cases_attribute.png" id="A3.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:419/469;" width="419" height="469" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span><span id="A3.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attribute recognition examples.</span>
(a) Mirror housing color; (b) tabletop material; (c) logo shape.
Correct answers and their corresponding options are highlighted in green.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Counting.</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Questions ask for the number of entities, object parts, or repeated patterns.
The examples below cover repeated images on a menu, people seated on a bench,
and pockets on a shirt.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/benchmark_cases_counting.png" id="A3.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/533;" width="476" height="533" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 6: </span><span id="A3.F6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Counting examples.</span>
(a) Eight burger images on a menu; (b) three people seated inside a shelter;
(c) two chest pockets on a shirt.
Each question requires an open-ended numerical answer.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Text Recognition (OCR).</h4>

<div id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Questions require transcribing text on signs, vehicles, clothing, printed materials, and product labels.
The examples below include a road sign, Japanese lettering on a truck,
and Chinese text on a bottle label.
Answers retain the original text visible in the image, regardless of the question language.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/benchmark_cases_ocr.png" id="A3.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/533;" width="476" height="533" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span><span id="A3.F7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Text recognition examples.</span>
(a) A supplementary road sign; (b) lettering on a truck’s rear door;
(c) the largest Chinese text on a bottle label.
Reference transcriptions are shown in green.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Additional Error Analysis</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section complements Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Error analysis ‣ 5 Experiments on ZoomGain Bench ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Per-model consistency.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Every evaluated model over-selects global-view errors:
they receive 65.0–78.2% of each model’s incorrect choices,
against 52.3–57.8% expected under uniform choice among the distractors of each question.
For the four closed-source models, which took no part in constructing the benchmark,
the shares are 75.7% versus 57.4%.
Their selection rate of a global-view error also rises with how consistently it arose during construction,
from 13.4% when given by one or two of the 30 full-image answers
to 35.2% when given more than ten times.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Controlling for option position.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Models prefer some option positions over others.
Normalizing by the average selection rate of each option position,
global-view errors are still selected 1.34 times as often as expected,
and 1.46 times when they also coincide with blind guesses,
compared with 0.52 and 0.55 times for blind guesses and visual evidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Below-chance accuracy of Qwen3-VL-8B.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Only 1.5% of Qwen3-VL-8B’s answers to attribute questions cannot be parsed,
so its below-chance accuracy does not stem from formatting failures.
Instead, 67.5% of its incorrect choices fall on global-view errors, against 54.0% expected.
Its responses typically claim to inspect the target closely
and then state a plausible but incorrect attribute,
for example describing a dark blue backpack as black.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Errors on open-ended questions.</h4>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Counting errors are mostly near misses:
71.6% of incorrect numeric answers are off by exactly one,
and 67 of the 94 counting questions have a ground truth of at most three,
so the difficulty lies in resolving a few small instances rather than in enumerating many objects.
For OCR, among transcriptions without full credit,
29.1% remain close to the reference, with a character-level similarity of at least 0.5;
10.1% omit part of the target text or include adjacent text;
and at least 13.4% transcribe other text in the scene instead of the target,
as identified by matching predictions against the scene descriptions generated during construction.
Most of the remaining transcriptions bear little resemblance to the reference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Representative Failure Cases</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix E Representative Failure Cases ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows representative failures discussed in Section <a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Error analysis ‣ 5 Experiments on ZoomGain Bench ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/error_cases.png" id="A5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/450;" width="476" height="450" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span><span id="A5.F8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Representative failures on ZoomGainBench.</span>
Each case shows the full image with the queried detail outlined in red,
an enlarged view of that region,
and the responses of the 56 evaluations (28 models <math id="A5.F8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> 2 languages).
(a) Nearly all evaluations name Bauer, a hockey equipment brand, instead of the NHL logo,
while the blind guesses (Reebok, Nike) are never chosen.
(b) The white tote bag is taken for a plastic bag;
the visual-evidence distractors, drawn from the black bag on her shoulder
and from another pedestrian’s purse, are never chosen.
(c) Most evaluations (46/56) call the white object on the truck’s dashboard orange,
likely the color of the vest worn by the worker in front of the truck.
(d) The salient reflected silhouettes draw choices away from the smaller crane at the base of the mast.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>ZoomGainBench Evaluation Settings</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All non-agentic models use the same system prompt as ZwZ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2026)</a></cite>,
which asks the model to reason before placing its final answer within
<span id="A6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;answer&gt;</span> and <span id="A6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;/answer&gt;</span> tags.
The user message contains the full image and the question with its options, if applicable.
Counting questions additionally request Arabic numerals, while OCR questions request
only the transcription within the answer tags, preserving capitalization, spacing,
punctuation, and symbols.
The Chinese version replaces the question stem while retaining the options and formatting instructions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Qwen models, ZwZ, and Vision-OPD use a temperature of 0 and a maximum output length
of 2,048 tokens, with native thinking disabled via <span id="A6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">enable_thinking=false</span>.
MiMo-VL-7B-RL uses the same temperature and output limit, with <span id="A6.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/no_think</span>
appended to the question.
GLM-4.6V and GLM-5.3-Flash use a temperature of 0 and output limits of 4,096 and
8,192 tokens, respectively; their requests also set <span id="A6.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">enable_thinking=false</span>.
Kimi-K3 is evaluated with thinking enabled, a temperature of 0, and an output limit
of 8,192 tokens.
GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6-Sol, Gemini-3.6-Flash, and Claude-Opus-5 use an output limit of
4,096 tokens and retain the provider defaults for temperature and thinking mode.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The four agentic models use their native reasoning and tool-use prompts with
multi-turn image interactions, all at a temperature of 0.
The per-turn output limits are 10,240 tokens for DeepEyes and PixelReasoner,
20,480 for DeepEyesV2, and 2,048 for Thyme.
The total output budget is 32,768 tokens per question.
DeepEyes, DeepEyesV2, and PixelReasoner allow up to 11 turns, while Thyme allows 5;
the tool-call limit is 10 for all except PixelReasoner, which allows 4.
Generic answer-format instructions that conflict with the native agentic protocols are removed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Training and Evaluation Settings</h2>

<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both datasets are trained with direct RL using GRPO,
with a batch size of 64, 8 rollouts per question, and one epoch (140 steps),
and the checkpoint at step 140 is evaluated.
For both ZwZ and ZoomGain, we use a learning rate of <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>,
no KL regularization, and a maximum response length of 2,046 tokens.
ZwZ images retain their native bounding-box overlays, whereas ZoomGain uses the original images.
For ZwZ, we follow the official reward definitions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2026)</a></cite>.
For ZoomGain, rewards follow the ZoomGainBench scoring rules:
multiple-choice and counting questions receive a reward of 1 for an exact match
on the selected option or predicted integer, respectively, and 0 otherwise.
OCR questions receive their ANLS score as the reward if it is at least <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.7</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.7</annotation></semantics></math>,
and 0 otherwise.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For the training experiments, all models are evaluated with chain-of-thought prompting and a temperature of 0.
Within each benchmark, base and trained models share the same prompt profile and output limit:
2,048 new tokens for all benchmarks except BabyVision, PerceptionBench, and O3-Bench,
which use 8,192 tokens and are scored by GPT-5.5 as the answer judge.
MMVP is scored by paired accuracy, CV-Bench by its official balanced score,
and MME-RealWorld on 1,919 questions.
VisualProbe is reported as the question-weighted average of its easy (141), medium (268), and hard (106) splits.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Global-to-Zoom Evidence and QA Construction Examples</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A8.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Appendix H Global-to-Zoom Evidence and QA Construction Examples ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>–<a href="#A8.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ Appendix H Global-to-Zoom Evidence and QA Construction Examples ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>
illustrate the construction process in Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Global-to-Zoom Evidence and QA Construction ‣ 3 ZoomGain Data Construction Pipeline ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>
for the three question types.
Each example shows the paired views and caption excerpts,
selected entries from the original incremental fact list,
and how one fact leads to a local QA pair and then a global QA pair.
Green text marks details newly described in the zoomed-view caption;
purple text highlights the local and global target references.
The zoomed views use the original pipeline crops.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/dual_caption_attribute.png" id="A8.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/466;" width="476" height="466" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span><span id="A8.F9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Attribute QA construction example.</span>
The global-view caption mentions logos on a visor without specifying their shapes.
The zoomed-view caption identifies a small star-shaped logo.
This fact supports a shape question, which is rewritten using the global referring expression
while preserving the answer.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A8.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/dual_caption_counting.png" id="A8.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/466;" width="476" height="466" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span><span id="A8.F10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Counting QA construction example.</span>
The global-view caption describes food images on digital menu boards without giving a count.
The zoomed-view caption identifies eight burger images arranged in two rows of four.
The selected fact yields a counting question with the same answer in both views.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A8.F11" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/dual_caption_ocr.png" id="A8.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/466;" width="476" height="466" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 11: </span><span id="A8.F11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OCR QA construction example.</span>
The global-view caption describes a bottle with a blue label without transcribing its text.
The zoomed-view caption reads the Chinese characters on the label.
The selected text fact supports a local OCR question, which is rewritten to identify
the bottle in the full image while retaining the original transcription as the answer.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Quality Verification Examples</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A9.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ Appendix I Quality Verification Examples ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> and <a href="#A9.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ Appendix I Quality Verification Examples ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>
show candidate QA pairs rejected by the two verification stages
in Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Quality Verification and Multi-Source Distractors ‣ 3 ZoomGain Data Construction Pipeline ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.
Crop-based verification checks whether the image supports the generated reference answer,
while blind verification filters questions whose answers are predictable without an image.
All questions, candidate answers, and vote counts are taken from the original generation records.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A9.F12" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/crop_verifier_rejections.png" id="A9.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/435;" width="476" height="435" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 12: </span><span id="A9.F12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Examples rejected by crop-based verification.</span>
The captions incorrectly describe (A) the race-car digit as “3” instead of “8”
and (B) the door handle as silver instead of white.
Both verification models give the visually supported answer in all 10 samples,
yielding zero matches to the generated reference answer and failing the 6/10 threshold.
The original crop inputs have no red anchor markers;
orange boxes and enlarged details are added only for display.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A9.F13" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.14076v1/blind_verifier_rejections.png" id="A9.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/435;" width="476" height="435" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 13: </span><span id="A9.F13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Examples rejected by blind verification.</span>
The reference answers, (A) drumsticks and (B) steam, are supported by the images,
but are also predictable from the questions alone.
Without images, the three models obtain 30/30 and 29/30 reference matches in total,
respectively, with every model meeting the rejection threshold of at least 3/10 matches.
The images and blue crop boxes are shown only for the reader;
no images are supplied to the blind models.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Prompts Used in Data Construction</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section provides the prompts for the roles described in Section <a href="#S3" title="3 ZoomGain Data Construction Pipeline ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>,
plus anchor enumeration, marked/unmarked zoomed-view captioning, and
<span id="A10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">EDGE_REWRITER</span> from Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Complete Algorithm and Additional Implementation Details ‣ ZoomGain: Mining Global-to-Zoom Perception Gaps for Fine-Grained Visual Supervision" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.
Templates are taken from <span id="A10.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">zoom_inc_pipeline/prompts.py</span>; view-dependent instruction blocks
are taken from their callers in <span id="A10.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pipeline.py</span>.
Sample-specific placeholders such as <span id="A10.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{anchor}</span>, <span id="A10.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{question}</span>, and <span id="A10.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{reference}</span>
are filled at runtime. JSON braces are shown as literal braces rather than Python string escapes.
A line of the form <span id="A10.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;&lt;&lt;INSERT: NAME&gt;&gt;&gt;</span> denotes exact insertion of the named block below,
allowing shared instructions to be printed once without omitting their content.
The insertion notation is for presentation only and is not sent to the models.</p>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">View-specific inputs.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">CAPTION1</span> receives the full image with the crop region marked.
<span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">CAPTION2</span> receives an unmarked zoomed view, while <span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">CAPTION2_ANCHOR_MARKED</span>
prepends marker-specific instructions to the same caption template.
The local anchor rule in QA generation is selected according to whether the zoomed view has an anchor marker.
<span id="A10.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">EDGE_REWRITER</span> receives the crop and the full image with its crop region marked;
a candidate box on the crop can additionally locate the referent being audited.
Crop solvers answer the local question; full-image and blind solvers answer the global question,
with no image supplied for blind answering.
The Kimi format instruction is appended to its open-answer requests.
Visual distractor generation uses the appropriate crop/full-view rules.
MCQ verification sees the crop, local question, global question as context, and assembled choices.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.1 </span>Shared instructions</h3>

<section id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">SPATIAL_FRAME_RULES</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SPATIAL FRAME CONTRACT — apply to every direction word you read or write:</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">- LEFT/RIGHT BETWEEN OBJECTS uses the viewer’s frame of the image: ’the person to the left of the sign’ means left as seen by the viewer. Never mirror-compute the reference object’s own left/right when locating one object relative to another. When such a phrase is load-bearing, prefer explicit wording such as ’on the left side of the image’.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">- BODY PARTS are anatomical, never viewer-relative: ’right hand’ always means the person’s own right hand. Derive the side from the person’s facing direction, never from raw image position: facing the camera -&gt; the right hand appears on the viewer’s LEFT; facing away from the camera -&gt; the right hand appears on the viewer’s RIGHT; facing image-left -&gt; the left side of the body is toward the camera; facing image-right -&gt; the right side of the body is toward the camera. If the facing direction is not clearly visible, never use left/right body-part wording; identify the part another way (by what it holds or touches, or with explicit viewer wording such as ’the hand on the left side of the image’).</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">- FRONT/BEHIND is NEVER a depth word. Scene depth must be written only as ’closer to the camera (than X)’ / ’farther from the camera (than X)’ / ’beyond X from the camera’s viewpoint’. The words front/behind are reserved exclusively for the intrinsic front/back sides of people, animals, and vehicles whose facing you have already stated: ’in front of the seated man’ is the side his face and chest point toward, and ’behind him’ is his back side, regardless of distance to the camera.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">- DEPTH-FLIP TRAP (the most common mistake — check every sentence): when the camera sees a person’s BACK, that person faces AWAY, so objects deeper in the scene are IN FRONT of that person, and objects between the camera and the person are behind them. Writing ’behind the man’ for a sign that lies beyond a man seen from the back is WRONG — write ’in front of the man (farther from the camera)’ or ’farther from the camera than the man’. The same flip applies to seated crowds watching something away from the camera.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">- For objects with no inherent front (poles, boxes, trees, candles, signs), never use front/behind at all; use camera-distance or image-position wording.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">- VEHICLE AND BUILDING PARTS use part terms fixed to the object itself: ’the cab end’, ’the rear of the trailer’, ’the side facing the camera’, ’the entrance side’. Never call a vehicle end ’front’ unless it is the actual forward/cab end of that vehicle.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">- GROUPS and entities whose facing cannot be determined: use the viewer frame with explicit image wording (’in the upper-left part of the image’, ’farther from the camera’), never intrinsic terms.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">- WHOSE FRAME ’THE IMAGE’ MEANS. Image-frame wording — ’in the upper-left part of the image’, ’near the left edge of the image’, ’图像左侧’ — always refers to the FULL photograph, and to nothing else.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">CROP_FRAME_CAVEAT</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">CROP FRAME CAVEAT:</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">- Your view is a window cut out of the middle of a larger photograph, so its borders are not the photograph’s borders and its left side is not the photograph’s left side. A position read off this view may be stated only as local to it, never as image-frame wording.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">- A FRAME SIDE IS ONLY HONEST NEAR AN EDGE. ’on the left side of the image’ is worth saying about something in the outer third of the photograph; for anything nearer the middle it reads as a claim the object is not where it is, and a solver scanning that side will not find it. When the target sits toward the centre, locate it against a named object instead — ’just right of the fire hydrant’, ’in front of the bus shelter and a little to its left’ — which stays true wherever the frame is drawn. You cannot see where this crop sits in the photograph, so when in doubt prefer the named object.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">- FRAME SUPERLATIVES REQUIRE THE WHOLE PHOTOGRAPH. leftmost, rightmost, topmost, bottommost, far left, far right, 最左, 最右, 最上, 最下, 最顶, 最底 assert that nothing of the kind lies further out, which only a view of the entire photograph can establish. Without that view do not write one in either language. Bounded superlatives inside one named host (’the bottom word on the blue sign’) are unaffected.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">- A HOST’S OWN CORNER NEEDS THAT CORNER IN VIEW. ’the bottom right corner of the window’, ’the top of the sign’, ’货架最下层’ name a position inside another object, and they are only true if THAT object’s edge on that side is visible here. When the host runs past the border, the corner you are looking at is the CROP’s corner, not the host’s, and the phrase points at something else entirely in the full photograph: a bookcase cropped to its top two shelves makes ’the book at the bottom of the bookcase’ name a green spine on the second shelf, while the bookcase’s real bottom shelf holds a red one. Use such a phrase only when you can see where the host ends on that side; otherwise identify the thing by what it is attached to, what is next to it, or its own visible attributes.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">KIMI_FINAL_ANSWER_TAG</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Begin your reply with the words The answer is, then put only your final answer inside &lt;answer&gt;&lt;/answer&gt;. For example: The answer is &lt;answer&gt;answer here&lt;/answer&gt;.</span>
</span></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.2 </span>Scene captioning and anchor grounding</h3>

<section id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">SCOUT_CAPTION</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Describe this image thoroughly. Then list every distinct, individually identifiable object or structure you can see (buildings, boats, vehicles, people, signs, statues, gates, bridges, etc.). Do not list background materials such as sky, water, grass, foliage or pavement as objects.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Direction wording: give every position in the image frame (’on the left side of the image’, ’in the lower-right foreground’). Express depth only as foreground / background / closer to or farther from the camera. Never use ’in front of’ or ’behind’ a person, animal, or vehicle to mean nearer to or farther from the camera, and never name a person’s own left/right body side.</span>
</span></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PHRASE_REWRITE</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">You are preparing referring expressions for a visual grounding model.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Below is a description of an image. Extract up to {max_phrases} candidate landmark objects and rewrite each as a SELF-CONTAINED English referring phrase that would pick out exactly one object instance for someone looking at the image.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Rules:</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">- Each phrase must denote exactly ONE object instance. Add a position word (left / center / right, foreground / background) or a color/size attribute whenever the bare noun could match several instances.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">- Position words inside a phrase must be IMAGE-FRAME words only: left / center / right, upper / lower, foreground / background, closest to the camera. NEVER locate a candidate with ’in front of’, ’behind’, ’ahead of’, or ’beyond’ another object or person — depth intent is ambiguous and grounding models disagree on it. Never use a person’s own left/right body side, and never locate one object through another object that the description places at a clearly different depth.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">- Only concrete, discrete objects: buildings, boats, vehicles, signs, towers, gates, statues, distinct groups. NEVER: sky, water, grass, trees, foliage, pavement, shadows, reflections, generic crowds.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">- Phrases must rely only on properties visible in the description; do not invent.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">- NEVER use written text, letters, logos or brand names read from the image as a qualifier (small text is unreliable at low resolution).</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">- Output strict JSON only:</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.12.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.12.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.12.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p12" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">{"phrases": [{"phrase": "...", "head_noun": "...", "qualifier_type": "position|color|size|none"}]}</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.13.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.14.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p14.1" class="ltx_p">Image description:</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.15.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">{caption}</span>
</span></span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GROUND_NORM1000</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">

<section id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ANCHOR_INSTANCE_CHECK</span>.</h4>

<div id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Find EVERY distinct visible instance of the concrete object category "{noun}" in this image crop. Include partially visible instances.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For each instance, draw one tight bounding box around only its visible extent. Do not infer or include hidden parts. Use integer coordinates normalized from 0 to 1000 in [x1, y1, x2, y2] order.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Return exactly one JSON object with these fields:</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">- "count": a non-negative integer equal to the number of detected instances.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">

<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">- "instances": a JSON array containing exactly "count" objects.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">

</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"> </span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10.1.3" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">

<span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">  - "description": a short, neutral, answer-free visual description.</span>
</span></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_pruned_first ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;"></span></span></span><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_inline-block" style="width:345.0pt;">  <span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_verbatim ltx_inline-block" style="width:333.0pt;"><span id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12.1.1" class="ltx_inline-logical-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_top" style="width:333.0pt;">
